body:
Can you test _without_ `--clean` or `-u NONE` (which skip _all_ runtime files, in particular all syntax scripts, so this is hardly unexpected behavior)? 

It's only a bug if it breaks with `nvim -u minrc.vim main.go`.
Maybe we should just internalize the definitions already.

With `nvim -u minrc.vim main.go`, things look a bit different because tree-sitter highlighting kicks in for me (only `Println` ends up being highlighted), but the symptoms are similar. The `String` and `Function` highlights are cleared.

The `scriptnames` sequence goes like:

```
init.vim
colorscheme
...
syntax/syntax.vim
syntax/synload.vim
...
```

`syntax/syncolor.vim` appears only after manually calling `:colo` or `:set bg`.
But I can reproduce that; `syncolor` is not loaded in the startup sequence at all (with vim color schemes; it _is_ with Lua color schemes).
However, I don't see a difference with my color scheme; `desert.vim` is apparently just a bad one (mixing up `guifg` and `ctermfg`, for one...)

I use a color scheme where only the "preferred highlight groups" from `:help group-name` are defined (e.g. `Constant`, `Identifier`, `Statement`, etc.), and other "minor highlight groups" rely on the default linking to the corresponding preferred group.

> ```
> if (params.use_vimrc == NULL || !strequal(params.use_vimrc, "NONE")) {
>     // Source syncolor.vim to set up default UI highlights if the user didn't
>     // already enable a colorscheme
>     if (!get_var_value("g:colors_name")) {
>       source_runtime((char_u *)"syntax/syncolor.vim", DIP_ALL);
>     }
> ```
> 
> This check is wrong as colorschemes might not load syncolor (not all do `syn en`)

Yes I suppose it is. I made the (apparently incorrect) assumption that colorscheme files would be responsible for defining all of the highlights, so sourcing syncolors.vim after a colorscheme was already loaded would only override already set highlights. 

>I use a color scheme where only the "preferred highlight groups" from :help group-name are defined (e.g. Constant, Identifier, Statement, etc.), and other "minor highlight groups" rely on the default linking to the corresponding preferred group.

*A* solution would be to move the `exists('g:colors_name')` guard around [lines 35-57 in `syncolor.vim`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/syntax/syncolor.vim#L35-L57) but let the rest of it still be sourced. This would create those default links in every case. Though this strikes me as just further hackiness...

>Maybe we should just internalize the definitions already.

I am all for this. Let's knock out this highlighting headache once and for all.

issue.body:
Remove syncolor.vim in favor of defining the default highlight groups directly in `init_highlight`. This approach provides a number of advantages:

1. The highlights are always defined, regardless of whether or not the syntax regex engine is enabled.
2. Redundant sourcing of syntax files is eliminated (synload.vim was often sourced multiple times based on how the user's colorscheme file was written).
3. The syntax highlighting regex engine and the highlight groups themselves are more fully decoupled.
4. Removal of the confusing `:syntax on` / `:syntax enable` dichotomy (they now both do the same thing).

This approach also correctly solves a number of bugs related to highlighting (#15176, #12573, #15205).

@bfredl
